UPSTREAM: soc/intel/fsp_broadwell_de: Add fixed VT-d MMIO range to the resources FSP initializes the VT-d feature on Broadwell-DE and assigns an address space to the MMIO range. coreboot's resource allocator needs to be aware of this fixed resource as otherwise the address can be assigned to a different PCI device. In this case addresses are overlapped and the VT-d range is not accessible any more. To deal with it the right way add a fixed MMIO resource to the resources list if VT-d BAR is enabled. TEST=Booted into Linux and checked coreboot log for resource assignment. Change-Id: I3d03be1e904e159e5e0ce44e0ab826b7367d05fc Signed-off-by: Martin Roth <martinroth@chromium.org> Original-Commit-Id: 1a22d3bc7e56e25ef2674bfdfbe6910a9e8a9372 Original-Change-Id: I626ac17420eadc0b49031e850f0f40b3b221a098 Original-Signed-off-by: Werner Zeh <werner.zeh@siemens.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/28672 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Nico Huber <nico.h@gmx.de> Original-Reviewed-by: Philipp Deppenwiese <zaolin.daisuki@gmail.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1236792

UPSTREAM: nb/amd/pi/00730F01: use MMIO and performance counters from AGESA This patch contain minimal set of changes to initial IVRS implementation to make it work reliably. UPSTREAM: i2c: dev: prevent ZERO_SIZE_PTR deref in i2cdev_ioctl_rdwr() i2cdev_ioctl_rdwr() allocates i2c_msg.buf using memdup_user(), which returns ZERO_SIZE_PTR if i2c_msg.len is zero. Currently i2cdev_ioctl_rdwr() always dereferences the buf pointer in case of I2C_M_RD | I2C_M_RECV_LEN transfer. That causes a kernel oops in case of zero len. Let's check the len against zero before dereferencing buf pointer. This issue was triggered by syzkaller. Signed-off-by: Alexander Popov <alex.popov@linux.com> Reviewed-by: Uwe Kleine-Knig <u.kleine-koenig@pengutronix.de> [wsa: use '< 1' instead of '!' for easier readability] Signed-off-by: Wolfram Sang <wsa@the-dreams.de> (cherry picked from commit 23a27722b5292ef0b27403c87a109feea8296a5c) BUG=b:114606649 TEST=Attempt i2c firmware update on cheza touchscreen Change-Id: Idc2228712a683ac49d54d7a8764583ed8b957ed8 Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1237049 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: i2c: refactor i2c_master_{send_recv} Those two functions are very similar, the only differences are that one needs the I2C_M_RD flag for its message while the other one needs the buffer casted to drop the const. Introduce a generic helper which allows to specify the flags (also needed later for DMA safe variants of these calls) and let the casting be done in the inlining functions which are now calling the new helper function. Make USB_PD_POWER_INFO detect inactive supplier Currently, CMD_USB_PD_POWER_INFO does not report a supplier if the available current is 0. This causes a dedicated charger (a barrel jack adapter) to be ignored by the command if it's not the active supplier. This change allows a supplier which has 0 current to be reported by the command as long as there is no other supplier with positive current on the same port. With this change, the host can detect a BJ adapter's physical presence regardless of its charging status. In other words, a supplier with positive current always supersedes whatever supplier with zero current. Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:841944,b:111667665,b:111777351 BRANCH=none TEST=Verify ectool usbpdpower 1 return 'Port 1: Disconnected' and 'Port 1: SNK (not charging)' without and with a BJ adapter connected respectively on Fizz. chgmgr: Allow charge_manager_update_charge to accept NULL Currently, charge_manager_update_charge does not handle NULL pointer for struct charge_port_info any differently. It's not sanity-checked either (thus memory access violation can occur). This patch will make charge_manager_update_charge accept NULL pointer and set available current and voltage to zero. FAFT: Add steps to check WP switch position at boot/cur before changing WP state '_setup_ec_write_protect' function considers the Hardware write-protect state is enabled or disabled, only based on 'wpsw_boot' value (irrespective of 'wpsw_cur' value). When HW write-protect status is 'wpsw_boot = 0' & 'wpsw_cur = 1' + EC SW write-protect is enabled, '_setup_ec_write_protect' function skips the EC write-protect disabling loop. So firmware_SoftwareSync test is failing while trying to corrupt the EC RW section. So adding the steps to check both 'wpsw_boot' & 'wpsw_cur' values and based on these values flipping the HW WP state.
